description: Ultra-compressed communication mode. Cuts token usage ~75% by dropping filler, articles, and pleasantries while keeping full technical accuracy. Use when user says "caveman mode", "talk like caveman", "use caveman", "less tokens", "be brief", or invokes /caveman.

Given a description of a product feature or user need, design a clean interface specification including components, props, and interaction patterns. Focuses on TypeScript-first, accessible, composable UI design.

Given a description of a business domain or feature area, produce a clean domain model with entities, value objects, relationships, and invariants. Output TypeScript types and interfaces that reflect the domain language precisely.
Edit and improve a draft article or blog post. Improve clarity, flow, and precision. Cut filler, sharpen arguments, fix structure. Preserve the author's voice. Output the revised article only.

Safety guardrails for Claude Code git operations. Prevents accidental force pushes, commits to protected branches, or destructive operations without explicit confirmation. Enforces safe-by-default git hygiene in agentic coding sessions.

Triage a GitHub issue or pull request. Classify severity, identify affected area, suggest labels, check for duplicates, and recommend next action. Output structured triage notes ready to paste as a GitHub comment.

Enter Socratic grilling mode. Ask probing questions to stress-test the user's reasoning, assumptions, or design decisions. Do not give answers — only ask questions. One question at a time. Push until the reasoning is airtight or the flaw is exposed.

Analyse a codebase or architecture description and produce a prioritised improvement plan. Identify coupling, missing abstractions, scalability risks, and inconsistencies. Output actionable recommendations with rationale.

Guide a migration from an existing setup to Shoehorn. Analyse the current configuration, identify incompatibilities, and produce a step-by-step migration plan with code changes, risks, and rollback notes.

Operate as an Obsidian vault assistant. Help organise notes, suggest links between concepts, create MOCs (maps of content), and maintain consistent tagging and naming conventions across a personal knowledge base.

Generate a thorough QA plan for a given feature, component, or system. Cover happy path, edge cases, error states, accessibility, and performance. Output structured test cases ready for a QA engineer or automated test suite.

Given existing code and a goal, produce a detailed refactor plan before writing any code. Identify what changes, why, in what order, and what risks exist. Output a numbered plan for human review and approval before execution.

Given a concept or skill to teach, scaffold a set of progressive coding exercises from beginner to advanced. Each exercise should have a clear goal, starter code, hints, and a solution. Output ready-to-use exercise files.

Set up a pre-commit hook configuration for a project. Select appropriate hooks for the stack (linting, formatting, type-checking, secret scanning). Output a working .pre-commit-config.yaml and setup instructions.

Drive development using strict TDD. Write a failing test first, then the minimal implementation to pass it, then refactor. Never write implementation code without a failing test. Output test and implementation in alternating red-green-refactor cycles.

Convert a requirements document, PRD, or feature description into a set of well-scoped GitHub issues. Each issue should have a clear title, description, acceptance criteria, and suggested labels. Output ready-to-file issue markdown.

Convert a rough feature idea, user story, or brief into a structured Product Requirements Document. Include background, problem statement, goals, non-goals, requirements, open questions, and success metrics.

Triage a single bug report or feature request. Assess severity, reproduction steps, affected scope, and priority. Suggest the appropriate label set and next action. Output a triage summary ready to post as a GitHub comment.

Given a domain description or codebase, extract and define the ubiquitous language for that domain. Produce a glossary of terms with precise definitions, usage examples, and notes on terms to avoid. Align language between business and engineering.

Write a new skill file in the standard format. Given a description of the skill's purpose, produce a complete SKILL.md with frontmatter (name, description) and a clear, concise instruction body. Follow existing skill conventions.

Step back from implementation details and evaluate the bigger picture. Given code, a plan, or a problem, identify what the user might be missing at the system, product, or strategy level. Ask clarifying questions or surface assumptions that haven't been examined.
